sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293 cells: Flag-APLP2 pulled down myc-his-CaN, demonstrating preserved protein–protein interaction; surface expression not separately quantified by flow cytometry or ELISA but interaction requires correct trafficking.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly states the Flag tag was placed 'immediately after the signal sequence' of APLP2 in a full-length pCMV-Sport6 construct; the signal peptide spans residues 1–31 (landmark-authoritative), so insert_after_residue = 31, placing the tag at the extracellular mature N-terminus (residue 32 onward). Python confirmed residue_before = A (pos 31) and residue_after = G (pos 32). The tag is 662 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any structural constraint. L7 independently confirms the Flag-tagged construct is functionally expressed and retains CaN binding. L5 (PMC11910330): A Flag-tag was incorporated immediately after the signal sequence of APLP2 in pCMV-Sport6 using QuikChange mutagenesis, generating a full-length membrane-anchored APLP2 construct with the tag at the extracellular N-terminus (after the SP cleavage site at residue 31). L7 (same paper) reports that Flag-tagged APLP2 expressed in HEK293 cells retained the ability to interact with myc-his-tagged calcineurin (CaN).

sources.claim: A Flag-tag was incorporated immediately after the signal sequence of APLP1 and APLP2 in pCMV-Sport6 using the QuikChange lightning mutagenesis kit (Agilent).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 (PMC10398996) describe a C-terminal FKBP-HA tag on APLP2_763; residue 763 falls within the intracellular span (715–763), so this is an intracellular tag, not a surface site. L4 (PMC2607064) describes a C-terminally FLAG-tagged APLP2 in pCMVTag4A; same reasoning, intracellular. L6 (PMC11910330) describes APLP2-GFP (C-terminal GFP fusion); again intracellular. L3 (PMC2607064) states 'FLAG-tagged APLP2 constructs were generated' with no position stated; disqualified because insert_after_residue cannot be pinned. L8 (PMC12682140) lists 'pEF-APLP2-SNAP (aa 1–763)' in a reagent table with no explicit statement of where the SNAP tag is inserted; disqualified for the same reason. L7 is used as functional validation for L5 and does not independently ground a new site.

literature_other_positions.note: FKBP-HA tag fused to the C-terminus of APLP2_763 in N2a cells; residue 763 lies in the intracellular domain (715–763), so this is a cytoplasmic tag, not a surface tag.
